parts.ask: \(ABCOA\) is a semicircle, centre \(O\), diameter 10 cm. \(OB\) is an arc of a circle with centre \(A\) and radius 5 cm. Find the exact area of the shaded region \(R\), in the form \((a\sqrt{3} + b\pi)\) cm².
parts.method: Spot the equilateral triangle, then sector minus segment

steps.text: \(AO = 5\) and \(OB = 5\) (radii of the semicircle), and \(AB = 5\) (a radius of the arc centred at \(A\)). So triangle \(AOB\) is equilateral.
steps.why: Every length in the picture is 5 cm. That's the key to the whole question.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is \(60^\circ = \tfrac{\pi}{3}\). Angles on the straight line \(AOC\) add up to \(\pi\).

steps.text: \(R\) is the sector \(BOC\) of the semicircle, minus the thin segment between the straight line \(OB\) and the arc \(OB\), which bulges into the sector.

steps.why: Sector of the circle centred at \(A\), angle \(\angle BAO = \tfrac{\pi}{3}\), minus triangle \(AOB\).
Keep the bracket: subtracting the segment adds the triangle back.

slips: Not spotting that triangle \(AOB\) is equilateral, and so finding no angle at all. Others found \(\tfrac{\pi}{3}\) the long way, with Pythagoras and trigonometry.
Finding one sector, the triangle or the semicircle and stopping there.
Sign errors when subtracting the segment, because the segment itself has a subtraction inside it.
Trying integration or polar coordinates. Far harder than sectors and triangles.
